items.stem: A user asks Copilot about a document they have no permission to open. What happens?

options.text: Copilot does not return that content, because it respects existing permissions
options.rationale: Correct: Copilot honours the user's existing access; inaccessible data is not returned.

options.text: Copilot returns it because AI overrides permissions
options.rationale: Copilot does not override Microsoft 365 permissions.

options.text: Copilot returns it only if encrypted
options.rationale: Encryption adds protection; it does not grant access.
Copilot does not delete content in response to a query.

items.explanation: Correct: Copilot honours the user's existing access; inaccessible data is not returned.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about sensitivity labels and Copilot are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A Copilot output can inherit the sensitivity label of its source content
options.rationale: Correct: label inheritance carries protection to generated items.

options.text: For encrypted content, users need the EXTRACT usage right for Copilot to return the text
options.rationale: Correct: EXTRACT (plus VIEW) is required to return encrypted content.

options.text: Labels are irrelevant once Copilot is enabled
options.rationale: Labels remain a key protection layer with Copilot.

options.text: Applying a label removes all access controls
options.rationale: Labels add, not remove, protection and controls.

items.explanation: Correct: label inheritance carries protection to generated items.

items.stem: When should oversharing be remediated relative to enabling Copilot?

options.text: Before and as an ongoing activity, because Copilot can surface overshared data faster
options.rationale: Correct: remediate oversharing before and continuously, since AI amplifies the risk.
Copilot does not fix permissions automatically.
Internal oversharing is also a risk Copilot can amplify.

items.explanation: Correct: remediate oversharing before and continuously, since AI amplifies the risk.
